Marta (Marketing): Hey team - prepping launch materials and need a compact, defensible bench package we can cite. Requests:

1) Model: redwood/text-7b-v2 (latest build).
2) Variants: fp16 and int8 quantized.
3) Slices: short (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), long (>512), and rare-tokens tail.
4) Metrics: median latency (+95% CI), p99 latency, avg throughput (tokens/s), request-level estimated cost.
5) Conditions: cold-start vs warm-path, and the explicit warmup policy used.
6) Artifacts: anonymized raw payloads, small sample of model outputs, per-slice histograms, and a short reproducibility README with CLI/job spec.

Can eng/runtime run this sweep and drop artifacts to a GCS path by EOD Friday? Were doing webinar + blog and need figures + appendix.

Leo (eng-runtime): Clarifying qs: which sequence-length distribution should we use for each slice? and how many replicates for CI?

Marta (Marketing): Use realistic distribution: short-heavy (50%), medium (40%), long (9%), rare-tokens (1%). For CI use bootstrap 95% and at least 3 replicates. Deadline EOD Fri still stands.

Devon (eng-ml): For int8 runs I need to know the quant config: activation/weight scales and calibration method (per-channel or per-tensor). Also want to record model build hash and kernel flags in the artifact metadata.

Ashley (product): Add to output: sequence-length histograms per slice, stabilization/warmup curve (requests vs latency) and a clear note about what well claim in marketing copy (median+95% CI; p99 as conservative). Avoid single-run numbers.

Leo (eng-runtime): Plan: 3 replicates per slice per variant, deterministic seeds. We'll record per-request metrics and compute bootstrap CIs for the median and p99. Warmup probe: 50 sequential requests/per worker to capture stabilization. Estimated wall time ~5-7h on a single dedicated node. Will redact PII from payloads and include job spec + CLI invocations in README.

Marta (Marketing): Please include the exact CLI command. Also a CSV with PNG-ready charts (median + CI bars and p99 lines) so our designer can drop into slides.

runtime-bot: Job queued: bench-sweep/3123456789-1. ETA ~6h. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/bench-sweep/3123456789-1

Leo (eng-runtime): Example job spec we'll include: ```bash
runtime-bench --model redwood/text-7b-v2 --variants fp16,int8 --slices short,medium,long,rare --replicates 3 --warmup 50 --seed 2026 --out gs://redwood-marketing/bench/3123456789/
```
Full JSON job manifest + env/kernel metadata will be saved in artifacts.

Devon (eng-ml): We'll capture: model git hash, compilation kernel id, quant config file, sequence-length histograms, per-request KV cache hit flag, and CPU/GPU utilization traces.

Ashley (product): Marketing copy note: "Median latency reported with bootstrap 95% CI; p99 reported as a conservative tail metric. Benchmarks collected on redwood/text-7b-v2 serving build X (hash available in artifact). Warm path uses cached KV; cold path is first request after worker start."

Marta (Marketing): Nice. Two small asks before you run: 1) please include sample sizes per slice in the README and CSV, and 2) a one-paragraph lay explanation of variance sources for press (warmup, batching differences, cache hit variability, hardware neighbors).

Leo (eng-runtime): Affirmative. We'll include sample counts, CSV/PNG exports, and a short variance note. If we hit time pressure we can deliver a condensed "figures pack" first and the full appendix after launch. Ping here when artifacts upload.

runtime-bot: Artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-marketing/bench/3123456789/artifacts.tar.gz (README, CSVs, PNGs, job-manifest, checksums).

Marta (Marketing): Thanks! Will pull figures and sync with Ashley for copy. Please keep the job-manifest public only to internal folks.

Leo (eng-runtime): Uploaded and shared internal link. Posting the job-manifest snippet and exact CLI in the README now. Will join briefly tomorrow AM if you want a walk-through of the figures.

Marta (Marketing): That would be great. Closing the loop for now  thanks everyone. :rocket:
